newsitem.title: FRANCE: French truck strike hits Nestle plant in Dijon.
newsitem.headline: French truck strike hits Nestle plant in Dijon.

text.p: Nestle France, part of the Swiss Nestle group said on Wednesday it had shut down a chocolate confectionery plant in the eastern town of Dijon because of a truckers' strike that has blocked raw material deliveries to the plant.
The company is also planning to shut five dairy products plants by the end of the week.
"Production stopped at the Dijon plant today and the closure of five dairy plants is scheduled for the end of this week," a company spokesman said.
The Dijon plant employs 650 people. The dairy products plants are located in the southern, northern and western parts of the country, he said.
The spokesman said it was premature to estimate the potential financial loss for the company.
Striking truckers have been blockading French roads and fuel depots, disrupting the supply of raw farm materials and food products to plants and stores.
On Tuesday agro-food industry officials warned that the sector was temporarily shedding workers and could run up big losses if the strike went on.
